attendance: more than 1,200 attendees (2026 projection; prospectus also carries 2025 attendee demographics)
attendance_method: Downloaded the AM26 Exhibit/Sponsorship Prospectus PDF and extracted its text. Page with the IARS/SOCCA overview states verbatim: 'The 2026 Annual Meeting will attract more than 1,200 attendees from across the globe, including research scientists, clinicians, critical care specialists...'. This is a forward projection, not a count, hence LOW confidence. The same PDF carries '2025 ATTENDEES: DEGREES / YEARS IN PRACTICE / PRIMARY PRACTICE SETTING / GEOGRAPHICAL DATA' demographic breakdowns but gives no 2025 total headcount, so no retrospective figure is available. No separation of delegates from exhibitor staff is given, so the basis is UNSPECIFIED and I could not discount an exhibitor component.
ratio_rationale: Judged 40%, against ESCMID 40% and ASN 35% — society meetings whose core currency is submitted science. IARS is literally the International Anesthesia RESEARCH Society; the prospectus schedule lists five General Poster Sessions across a three-day meeting plus a 'Mini Orals Abstract Presentation' track and named 'Abstract Awards', which is a very high density of presentation slots for a ~1,200-person meeting. Small research-society meetings of this shape sit well above the teaching-course anchors (EuroPCR 6%) and near the research-dense end of the scale. Not pushed to the GSA 119% / ESPGHAN 155% end because the programme also carries substantial invited plenary and CME content.
programme_evidence: Prospectus schedule: five 'Poster Session' blocks across May 1-3 plus 'Mini Orals Abstract Presentation ... presentations in the poster hall', alongside plenary/symposium content and 'Abstract Award' sponsorships.
character_evidence: https://meetings.iars.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/AM26-Prospectus-final-11-25-25-compressed.pdf — sponsorable 'Abstract Awards', 'General Poster Sessions' and a 'Mini Orals Abstract Presentation' track imply an open call for abstracts.

character_evidence: Not confirmed on a loaded page — the isscr2025/2026 meeting sites, which carry the abstract deadlines, were unreachable.

attendance: attendance was 9,288 in 2022 (of which roughly a quarter are exhibitor staff)
attendance_method: Downloaded the SmileCon 2023 Exhibitor Prospectus PDF and extracted text. Under the heading 'Meet our attendees' / 'How many attendees will be there?' it states verbatim: 'In 2022, our attendance was 9,288—over a 20 percent increase'. I also pulled the SmileCon 2025 Sponsorship Prospectus (https://www.ada.org/-/media/project/ada-organization/ada/ada-org/files/education/smilecon/2024-files/2024exhibitor/ada_smilecon25_sponsorship_prospectus.pdf) which gives no total headcount but breaks the attendee mix down as DENTISTS 32% / DENTAL TEAM 26% / EXHIBITORS 26% / OTHER 12% / STUDENTS 6%. That 26% exhibitor share is the inflation to watch: the 9,288 headline is a total-onsite number including exhibitor staff, so the professional-delegate body is roughly 6,900. Note the event has since been renamed — ADA's site says the 2026 edition is the 'ADA Scientific Session, formerly known as SmileCon'.
ratio_rationale: Judged 4% of the 9,288 headline, against EuroPCR 6% and AAD 9% — and deliberately below both. SmileCon is the ADA's CE-and-trade-show event, not a research congress: its own prospectus sells 'Dental Central' (the exhibit hall) as the epicentre, brags that '95% of dentists surveyed visited Dental Central', and describes hands-on CE, a Friday Night Fest and an Opening Session with musical entertainment — the word 'abstract' does not appear anywhere in either prospectus I extracted. EuroPCR at 6% is the right shape of comparable (a teaching event where attendance says nothing about submitted science) and SmileCon is further from research than EuroPCR is. Discount applied: the only cohort I am subtracting is the 26% exhibitor staff, who cannot submit — I am NOT discounting the 6% students or the 12% 'other', who can. That leaves roughly 6,900 submitters-in-principle, so 4% of the 9,288 headline is about 5.4% of the people actually able to submit. Honest uncertainty: this could be 2% (a trade show with a token poster board) or 6% (a real if small scientific session inside the ADA Scientific Session, which is what the 2026 rename hints at); 4% is my most likely reading.
programme_evidence: 'thousands of dental professionals ... gather to celebrate all things dentistry'; sponsorable items are CE courses, lounges, parties and exhibit-hall activations. No abstract or poster sponsorship exists in either prospectus, unlike the IARS prospectus which sells 'Abstract Awards'.
character_evidence: https://www.ada.org/-/media/project/ada-organization/ada/ada-org/files/education/smilecon/2024-files/2024exhibitor/ada_smilecon25_sponsorship_prospectus.pdf — no call for abstracts anywhere in the prospectus; framing is CE, hands-on learning and exhibition.

attendance_method: The SAEM exhibitor-prospectus HTML page is a navigation shell with no figure on it, so I downloaded the linked SAEM Prospectus Book PDF (11.5MB) with curl and extracted the text. Three separate places state the figure: the cover line '3,900+ Emergency Medicine Professionals'; body text 'Each year, the SAEM Annual Meeting has steadily grown to over 3,900+ attendees'; and an Attendees stat block '3,900+ Annual Attendees'. This is the current (2026) prospectus — booth-staff pre-registration deadline is 30 April 2026. It says 'attendees', not delegates, and gives no exhibitor-staff split, so basis is UNSPECIFIED; the same PDF separately states SAEM has 10,600+ members. No inflation discount was possible.
ratio_rationale: Judged 45%, against ATS 50%, AAIC 50% and ECR 48% — academic society meetings whose central purpose is presenting original research, and where roughly half the room is on the programme. SAEM describes itself as 'the largest forum for the presentation of original education and research in academic emergency medicine', its abstracts are published as a full supplement of Academic Emergency Medicine, and its attendees are near-uniformly academic faculty, fellows and residents for whom presenting is the reason to travel. Nudged slightly below the ATS/ECR anchors because SAEM also runs a heavy didactic, career-development and residency-recruitment programme that brings non-presenting trainees into the room.
programme_evidence: SAEM's own abstracts page: 'The SAEM annual meeting is the largest forum for the presentation of original education and research in academic emergency medicine.'
character_evidence: https://www.saem.org/meetings-and-events/annual-meeting/annual-meeting-navigation/education/abstracts — a standing abstracts page with an open call and published Abstract Award Winners.

attendance_rung_name: society press release (distributed via Yahoo Finance)
attendance_method: Loaded the EAACI leadership press release 'EAACI Leadership Reflects on Record-Breaking Congress 2025'. It states verbatim: 'With over 7,600 delegates in attendance, EAACI Congress 2025 made headlines'. The congress ran 13-16 June 2025 at the Scottish Event Campus, Glasgow. The source says 'delegates', not registrants or total attendance, so I have tagged it DELEGATES rather than TOTAL_ONSITE; the release gives no exhibitor-staff or virtual breakdown, so no further discount was needed or possible. Retrospective and post-event, hence a count rather than a projection.
ratio_rationale: Judged 28%, sitting between EASL 24% and UEG 35% — large European specialty congresses that pair a very heavy taught programme with a big contributed poster hall. The EAACI release itself emphasises 'over 250 hours of lectures, workshops, and symposia', which is a teaching-forward description and argues against the ESCMID 40% / SOT 46% end; but allergy and clinical immunology is an academically dense field and EAACI runs a large abstract-driven poster and TPS programme, which puts it clearly above the clinical-cardiology anchor of ESC 15%. Because the figure is already a clean delegate count, no inflation discount was applied.
programme_evidence: 'The programme featured over 250 hours of lectures, workshops, and symposia' — a large taught core, run alongside EAACI's contributed abstract sessions.
character_evidence: https://eaaci.org/events_congress/eaaci-congress-2025/scientific-programme/session-type/ — the congress runs distinct session types including contributed abstract formats alongside invited symposia; an open call for abstracts exists each year.

attendance: 7,000+ executives across the ecosystem (organiser's own forward statement for ViVE 2027)
attendance_method: Loaded the official ViVE site (hlth.com/events/vive/) with curl and stripped the markup. It states verbatim: 'With 7,000+ executives across the ecosystem, ViVE 2027 is where healthcare's digital leaders meet to decide what's next.' The page's headline stat blocks ('Attendees 0 + / C-Level 0 + / Media Outlets 0 +') are JavaScript count-up animations that render as zero in a non-browser load, so the 7,000+ prose line is the only figure I could actually confirm. Search snippets assert '8,000+ attendees' for ViVE 2025 and '7,300' for 2024 from Chief Healthcare Executive, but that site 403s to WebFetch and returned an empty body to curl with a browser UA, so I am not reporting those. Basis UNSPECIFIED: 'executives' is not a delineated delegate count and a commercial event of this kind counts sponsor and vendor staff inside its headline.
ratio_rationale: Judged 0.5% — the new floor, and I am taking it because my honest reading is zero rather than because the floor forced me there (under the old 2% floor I wrote exactly that caveat; the lowered floor lets me state what I actually believe). This is not a 'wrong sort of attendee' judgement — it is that almost no contributed science happens at this meeting at all. ViVE is a commercial digital-health business event: its own site describes it as 'THE ONLY EVENT WHERE DIGITAL HEALTH EXECS GO TO DO BUSINESS', built around 1:1 matchmaking programmes ('Provider & Payer Connect', 'Investor Connect'), sponsors and a media-facing agenda. There is no call for abstracts, no poster hall and no proceedings. Even EuroPCR at 6% — our lowest counted anchor, and a teaching course where attendance says nothing about submitted science — is far more research-bearing than this. The 7,000+ headline is also exhibition-padded in the way the lowered floor anticipates. This row is logged so that the exclusion is on the record.
programme_evidence: Site navigation is Agenda / Sponsors / Attendee Networking / Matchmaking / 'Why ViVE — Audience Snapshot'; the programme is keynote, panel and dealmaking, with no scientific session types listed.
character_evidence: https://hlth.com/events/vive/ — no call for abstracts, no submission deadline and no author guidelines anywhere on the event site; speakers are invited executives.

attendance: 3,718 scientific attendees (overall total 4,837 including exhibitor booth personnel)
attendance_rung_name: exhibitor prospectus carrying retrospective registration demographics
attendance_method: asm.org/events/asm-microbe/exhibit failed on a TLS issuer-certificate error, so I downloaded the 2026 ASM Microbe Exhibitor Prospectus PDF (7.7MB) directly with curl and extracted the text. Its '2025 Registration Demographics' section gives a full registration-type table: Full Conference 1,641 / Post Doc 406 / Student 1,041 / Speaker/Conveners 314 / Exhibitor Full Conference 316 = 'Scientific Total 3,718'; then Exhibitor Booth Personnel 803, Non-Exhibiting Suppliers 6, One-Day 127, Other (Press/Vendor/Staff/Guests) 183 = 'Overall Total 4,837'. A footnote confirms '* Statistics are based on scientific attendees'. I have taken the Scientific Total as the headline precisely because the Overall Total is inflated by 803 booth staff; note the Scientific Total still contains 316 exhibitor full-conference registrations, a small residual inflation. Two caveats in the other direction, under the updated brief: ASM's own 'Scientific Total' excludes the 127 One-Day registrants, who are ordinary attendees able to submit, so 3,718 slightly understates the submitter population; and the large Student (1,041) and Post Doc (406) cohorts stay inside the headline, since trainees present. Virtual is listed as 'n/a', so nothing virtual is folded in. A separate marketing line in the same PDF says 'Engage with over 5,000 attendees across the microbial sciences' — that is a forward-looking 2026 sell and is recorded as an alt figure.
ratio_rationale: Judged 45% of the 3,718 scientific total, against SOT 46% and ESCMID 40% — basic and translational science meetings where the room is dominated by trainees who travel in order to present. ASM Microbe's own 2025 demographics make that case directly: 1,041 Student + 406 Post Doc + 799 Graduate Student career-level registrations, i.e. roughly two-fifths of the scientific body is at the career stage where a poster is the point of attending; 'Researcher' (1,427) and 'Student' (824) are the two largest job functions; and ASM sells the venue as the 'Exhibit & Poster Hall', a single co-located space. Kept just below SOT because ASM Microbe also carries a substantial clinical-microbiology practice audience (520 Clinical Lab Professionals) that attends for CE rather than to submit. The inflated 4,837 overall total was explicitly set aside in favour of the clean scientific figure.
programme_evidence: The prospectus repeatedly names the 'Exhibit & Poster Hall' as the meeting's centre and sells app access to 'the full meeting and speaker schedules, abstracts, exhibitor listings'; the demographic profile is overwhelmingly researchers and trainees.
character_evidence: https://s3.goeshow.com/asm/microbe/2026/documents/2026_ASM_Microbe_-Exhibitor_Prospectus.pdf — abstracts are a first-class object in the meeting app and the poster hall is a headline venue, implying an open call.

attendance: 2,615 total professional attendees (total attendance 4,528 including exhibitors and guests)
attendance_method: Downloaded the Optometry's Meeting 2026 Exhibitor Prospectus PDF with curl and extracted the text. Its 'MEET OUR ATTENDEES' page gives the 2025 breakdown verbatim: Doctors of Optometry 1,621 / Optometric Staff/Paraoptometrics 252 / Students 584 / Industry Professionals/Association Executives 49, then '2025 TOTAL PROFESSIONAL ATTENDESS 2,615' [sic] and 'TOTAL ATTENDANCE (includes exhibitors & guests) 4,528'. This is exactly the EUROSPINE-shaped trap the brief warns about: the 4,528 headline is 42% non-professional, so I have taken the 2,615 professional figure as the headline and logged the padded total as an alt figure. The 2026 edition runs 17-20 June in Phoenix.
ratio_rationale: Judged 3% of the 2,615 professional attendees, below EuroPCR 6% and well below AAD 9%. The reason is what happens at the meeting, not who attends it: the words 'abstract', 'poster', 'paper' and 'research' do not appear once in the entire 2026 prospectus (I grepped it — zero hits), and the AOA frames the event as 'four days of optometric continuing education and professional development, networking with industry thought-leaders, and an ophthalmic industry exhibit hall', with 'Eye Care Square' as the draw. EuroPCR at 6% is our anchor for a meeting whose attendance says nothing about submitted science, and this is a step further in that direction. I am NOT discounting the 584 students inside the 2,615 — students present abstracts, and at a meeting with a research track they would be among the likeliest to. The only discount applied is the legitimate one: the 4,528 headline was rejected because its extra 1,913 are exhibitors and guests, who cannot submit. Honest uncertainty: if Optometry's Meeting runs a poster session the prospectus simply never mentions, the true figure could be nearer 6%; 3% is what the evidence I loaded supports.
programme_evidence: 'four days of optometric continuing education and professional development ... and an ophthalmic industry exhibit hall'; zero occurrences of abstract/poster/research in the prospectus.
character_evidence: https://s2.goeshow.com/aoa/optometry/2026/documents/2582025123817_2026-FinalExhibitorProspectus.pdf — no call for abstracts and no research track described anywhere; the programme is CE courses plus exhibits.

attendance: more than 3,500 attendees and over 200 exhibitors
attendance_method: Loaded the ONS Congress Press Kit on ons.org. It states verbatim: 'ONS Congress is the largest and most comprehensive oncology nursing conference in the United States, bringing together more than 3,500 attendees and over 200 exhibitors for five days of education, networking, and innovation.' No year is attached — it is a standing descriptor, which is why the year field is unspecified and confidence is MEDIUM. A search snippet separately asserts 'more than 4,000 oncology nurses convened in Denver, CO' for the 2025 edition; I did not load a page carrying that sentence and am therefore not reporting it as a figure. The 3,500 is stated alongside, not inclusive of, the 200 exhibitors, but ONS does not say whether booth staff sit inside the 3,500, so the basis is UNSPECIFIED and no discount could be applied.
ratio_rationale: Judged 13%, essentially at the ASHP 12% anchor — the closest counted comparable in the list, being the other large US non-physician clinical-professional congress built on a broad CE programme with a contributed poster track published in the society's own journal. ONS has a genuine, structured open call (three categories: Evidence Based Practice/Quality Improvement, Research, and Industry Supported) and publishes 'ONS Congress Poster Abstracts' as an Oncology Nursing Forum article, so it is clearly above the pure trade/CE floor of EuroPCR 6% and AAD 9%. But it sits nowhere near the physician-researcher oncology anchors (SABCS 21%, WCLC 25%): the great majority of the 3,500 are practising oncology nurses attending for continuing education, and submitting is a minority activity concentrated among nurse scientists and QI leads.
programme_evidence: 'five days of education, networking, and innovation'; abstracts are accepted in EBP/QI, Research and Industry-Supported categories with 'top-scoring abstracts presented orally ... or as moderated poster presentations' — a selective contributed track inside a large CE programme.
character_evidence: https://www.ons.org/education-hub/events/ons-congress/abstracts — open call for the 2027 Congress, submissions accepted 10 August to 24 September 2026, three named categories.

attendance_method: Loaded the EURETINA Congress Daily report on the opening of the 25th Congress (Palais des Congres, Paris, 4-7 September 2025). It states 'over 11,000 registrants' and that this is 'the first time that the number of registrations for the annual Congress has surpassed 10,000'. Basis is UNSPECIFIED deliberately: the source says registrants, not delegates, and gives no split between clinicians, industry staff and any virtual cohort — a retina congress of this size carries a very large ophthalmic-industry presence that is almost certainly inside the number, so this headline should be treated as padded. A search snippet elsewhere cites 4,090 'registered attendees' for the same congress, which is a strikingly different metric; I could not confirm it on a loaded page and record it here only as a caution that the spread is large.
ratio_rationale: Judged 15%, at the ESC 15% anchor and below EASL 24%. EURETINA is a large clinical-specialty congress of exactly the ESC shape: a headline registrant count swollen by a heavy device and pharma presence, a programme dominated by invited instructional courses, symposia and surgical video sessions, and a free-paper/poster track that is real and sizeable but carried by a minority of the room. I could NOT discount the industry component because the source publishes no split, so this ratio is applied to an inflated base and is, if anything, generous on the low side deliberately. Retina specialists worldwide are a much smaller population than 11,000, which is itself evidence that a large share of the registrant count is not submitting clinicians.
programme_evidence: EURETINA's Paris 2025 programme overview lists instructional courses, symposia and surgical/video sessions alongside free-paper and poster sessions.
character_evidence: https://euretina.org/paris-2025/programme-overview-list-view/ — an annual open call for free papers and posters runs alongside a large invited instructional programme.

attendance: at least 2,000 participants expected (Milan 2026); the same document describes the meeting as bringing together more than 1,500 leaders
attendance_method: Downloaded the 'Application for Sponsorship and Exhibition, 2026 ISPE Annual Meeting' prospectus PDF (3.8MB) with curl and extracted the text. Two figures sit in the same document: the exhibition section states 'We expect at least 2,000 participants in Milan, Italy', and the 'Who Attends the ISPE' section states the meeting brings 'together more than 1,500 leaders representing industry, service providers, government/regulatory agencies, academia, consultants and students'. I have not averaged them: the 2,000 is the dated, venue-specific statement and is the headline; the 1,500 standing descriptor is logged as an alt figure. Both are UNSPECIFIED — neither separates delegates from exhibitor and sponsor staff, and given that 'industry/service provider' is the first audience ISPE names, the industry share here is large. Note ICPE is the former name; the society now brands it the ISPE Annual Meeting (42nd, Milan, 29 August - 2 September). Confidence is LOW because the headline is a pre-event expectation, not a count.
ratio_rationale: Judged 40%, at the ESCMID 40% anchor and just below SOT 46%. ICPE is a compact, single-discipline scientific society meeting whose entire reason for existing is contributed pharmacoepidemiological studies — the abstracts are published as a supplement of Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety and the poster hall is the meeting's substance rather than a sidebar, which is exactly the ESCMID/SOT shape. Held below the ATS 50% / ECR 48% top anchors for one specific reason visible in ISPE's own prospectus: 'industry, service providers ... consultants' are the first audiences named and the exhibition is pitched hard at CRO and pharma safety departments, so a meaningful slice of the 2,000 are commercial attendees who buy rather than submit. I could not quantify that slice — the prospectus publishes no split — so this ratio is applied to an undiscounted base.
programme_evidence: ISPE describes the meeting as convening pharmacoepidemiologists including 'the next generation of pharmacoepidemiologists' with a programme built on contributed research; abstracts are journal-published.
character_evidence: https://www.pharmacoepi.org/meetings/annual-conference/ — the annual meeting runs a standing open call for abstracts with published submission deadlines.

attendance: more than 2,000 delegates from over 120 countries
attendance_rung_name: post-meeting report / congress highlights by the organiser
attendance_method: Loaded UICC's own post-congress highlights piece with curl and read the raw text. It states twice, verbatim: 'more than 2,000 delegates from over 120 countries' and 'the event gathered over 2,000 delegates from more than 120 countries, including UICC members, researchers, healthcare professionals, private sector representatives and advocates'. This is a retrospective organiser report (A2), not a projection, and it says delegates. The congress ran 17-19 September 2024 in Geneva. The same page notes the online platform remained open afterwards for session replay, so there is a virtual tail, but the 2,000 is presented as the delegate body, not a virtual-inclusive total. A search snippet asserting a '1,750 on-site' split was not confirmed on any page I loaded and is not reported.
ratio_rationale: Not a judgement call — the organiser states the abstract figure directly, which the brief says beats any ratio. The same UICC page reads: 'The top abstracts among the more than 1,200 submitted to the World Cancer Congress were recognised in three categories: Best Scientific Study, Best Advocacy and Policy Report, and Best Fundraising Campaign.' 1,200+ submissions against 2,000+ delegates gives 60%. That is high but entirely consistent with the congress's character and with our own anchors: it sits between WCLC 25% and the small-specialty anchors GSA 119% / ESPGHAN 155%, and the reason is that UICC's three award categories show abstracts here are not only scientific studies — advocacy reports and fundraising campaigns are submissible, which drastically widens who in the room has something to submit. Note the figure counts SUBMISSIONS, not accepted presentations, so the presented-abstract count is lower.
programme_evidence: 'Select abstracts from the Congress are featured in a special edition of the International Journal of Cancer'; UICC thanks 'the Congress speakers, abstract presenters, committees, partners, co-hosts, sponsors, and exhibitors' — abstract presenters are named as a first-class constituency.
character_evidence: https://www.uicc.org/news-and-updates/news/uniting-cancer-control-highlights-world-cancer-congress-2024 — an open call producing 'more than 1,200 submitted', judged across Best Scientific Study, Best Advocacy and Policy Report and Best Fundraising Campaign categories.

A2/A3: americantelemed.org/events/nexus-annual-conference-expo/ loaded with dates (3-6 May 2025, New Orleans) and a one-line description, no headcount; ata-nexus.org/ loaded and gives no figure. A4: nothing from a venue or bureau surfaced. The only number in circulation — 'roughly 2,000 attendees' — comes from a third-party marketing blog (buzzboxmedia.com) and I could not confirm it against any ATA page, so I am not reporting it. Attendee-mix claims ('over half represent provider and care delivery organizations, more than a third are C-suite') also appeared only in snippets. Absence of evidence is not evidence the meeting is small — ATA Nexus is the field's flagship US telehealth conference with a full expo; it simply does not publish a headcount.
programme_evidence: ATA describes Nexus as 'built around the real-world challenges healthcare organizations face, where leaders, clinicians, researchers, innovators, policymakers, and industry partners come together to share what works' — a practice-and-policy programme with an expo, not a research congress. The submission route is a 'Call for Content Proposals & Research Abstracts', i.e. session proposals first and abstracts second.
character_evidence: https://ata-nexus.org/ — 'Call for proposals and research! Submit by Saturday, October 31, 2026', linking to 'Call for Content Proposals & Research Abstracts'. A real research-abstract route exists but is bolted onto a proposal-driven, curated programme.

attendance: 1,505 members in person plus 142 virtual attendees — 1,647 in total
attendance_method: Loaded the European Society of Coloproctology's own past-conference page for ESCP Dublin, 21-23 September 2022. It states '1505 members in person and 142 virtual attendees from across the globe' and describes 'over 400 presentations, symposiums, sessions, Q&As, guidelines, industry workshops and discussions'. REVISED under the updated brief: I originally headlined the 1,505 in-person figure and set the virtual cohort aside, which the new rule forbids — an abstract presented online still counts and a remote presenter is a presenter — so the headline is now the full 1,647 and the in-person subset is the alt. Neither number is padded in the way that matters: both are registered attendees, not exhibitor staff or exhibition footfall, so no discount applies. The year is the caveat: 2022 is the most recent edition for which ESCP publishes a count and it was a post-COVID-recovery year, so the current (Paris 2025 / Prague 2026) meeting is plausibly larger — an ESCP page cited in search for Nice 2018 claims 'over 1,800 delegates from more than 70 countries', which I did not load and therefore do not report.
ratio_rationale: Judged 30%, between EASL 24% and UEG 35% — European digestive-disease specialty societies of very similar shape and size profile, each pairing an invited guideline-and-masterclass core with a large contributed poster hall. ESCP is a 'Scientific Annual Meeting' by name, publishes an abstracts book through Wiley Online Library (Colorectal Disease), and is unusual among surgical societies in running large multicentre snapshot-audit collaboratives that generate a high volume of trainee-authored submissions — which argues for the upper half of that band. Held below UEG because the ESCP page's own summary of the meeting leads with 'symposiums, sessions, Q&As, guidelines, industry workshops', a teaching-forward description, and well below ATS 50% because a surgical society's attendance includes many consultants who come for technique and guideline sessions rather than to present.
programme_evidence: 'over 400 presentations, symposiums, sessions, Q&As, guidelines, industry workshops and discussions' — a mixed programme, with a separately published abstracts book.
character_evidence: https://www.escp.eu.com/conference-and-events/past-conferences/escp-dublin-21-23-september-2022 — the meeting publishes an abstracts book via Wiley Online Library, implying an annual open call for abstracts.

attendance_method: The EWMA conference overview and the pre-event news item carry no figures, so I listed ewma.org/news/ with curl, found the post-meeting item, and loaded it. Dated 26 May 2026, it reports EWMA-DEWU 2026 (Bremen, 6-8 May 2026) verbatim as: '6,364 participants from 81 countries / 955 oral presentations / 661 e-Posters / 166 exhibitors'. Basis is UNSPECIFIED and the figure should be treated as padded: it says participants, not delegates, gives no exhibitor-staff split despite 166 exhibiting companies, and — importantly — 2026 was a JOINT conference with DEWU, the German wound union, which inflates it relative to a standalone EWMA year. I also pulled the EWMA-DEWU 2026 Branding Catalogue PDF (2.3MB); it contains sponsorship item quantities ('7,000 branded recycled plastic water bottles', 'Price based on serving 1,000 participants') which are procurement numbers, not attendance, and I have not converted them.
ratio_rationale: Judged 15%, at the ESC 15% anchor — a large clinical congress with a heavy taught programme and an industry-padded headline, where the contributed track is substantial in absolute terms but a minority of the room. Here the arithmetic is unusually well grounded because EWMA publishes its own presentation counts: 661 e-Posters alone is 10.4% of the 6,364 participants, and the 955 'oral presentations' are mostly invited faculty across 200+ sessions, with a free-paper subset on top; adding a plausible contributed share of those orals lands the submitted-abstract population right around 15%. I could only partially discount the inflation — the 166 exhibitors' booth staff and the DEWU co-branding both sit inside the 6,364 with no published split, so if anything the true share of submitters among genuine EWMA delegates is higher than 15%.
programme_evidence: EWMA 2026 delivered '955 oral presentations' and '661 e-Posters' across 'more than 200 sessions' with 'approximately 150 leading industry exhibitors' — a large invited teaching programme running alongside a genuine contributed e-Poster track.
character_evidence: https://ewma.org/news/a-record-breaking-attendance-at-ewma-2026ewma-dewu/ — 661 e-Posters presented, and the EWMA conference app gives delegates access to 'abstracts' as a first-class object, evidencing an annual open call.
